name: Sentinela
title.cpu: “{name}” has used a lot of CPU for 5 minutes
title.imitation: “{name}” looks like a system program, but isn’t one
title.replaced: The program of “{name}” was deleted after it started
title.autostart: A new program starts by itself: “{name}”
why.cpu: It has used more than 80 % of a core all the time for 5 minutes. It lives in {place}.
why.memory: Its memory has grown steadily for 10 minutes: it may be a leak. It lives in {place}.
why.imitation: Its name is that of a system or kernel process, but its program lives in {place}.
why.replaced: Its program file was deleted or replaced while it runs, and it lives in {place}.
why.autostart: It was added to the programs that start with your session.
fact.deleted: Its file was deleted or replaced after it started
analyzed: What Lumo analyzed (on this computer, without the internet)
analysis.noModel: Rules only: no local model chosen.
analysis.battery: Rules only: the computer was on battery.
analysis.running: The local model is analyzing it…
analysis.failed: The local model didn’t answer: rules only.
analysis.rejected: The local model’s answer wasn’t valid and was discarded.
modelNormal: Lumo saw nothing unusual, but the rule still fired: take a look yourself.
youDecide: Lumo suggests; you decide. No action runs by itself.
trigger.cpu: High CPU sustained (more than 80 % for 5 min)
trigger.network: Program from no package connecting to a new server
trigger.replaced: Program whose file was deleted or replaced after it started
trigger.autostart: Program that starts by itself and I don’t recognize
settings.onHint: Watches the processes and tells you when something looks wrong. Off by default.
settings.footer: It uses only the local model: nothing leaves this computer.
settings.modelFooter: The model runs only on this computer, without network, on a private socket only LordOS can use. Without a model, Sentinela still warns you with its rules.
settings.pickModel: Choose which installed model analyzes the alerts.
settings.noModel: No model installed: download one to have each alert explained. Its size and SHA-256 are checked.
settings.triggersFooter: Only your own processes are watched, every 10 seconds.
settings.engineMissing: Not installed: it is downloaded with the first model.
settings.seesText: Name, origin, who started it, CPU, memory and the summary of its package. Never the contents of files, passwords, the arguments it was started with or the text of windows.
settings.ignoredFooter: Sentinela doesn’t warn about these programs again.
title.vmSandbox: The machine “{name}” runs with a weaker sandbox
title.vmLeak: The machine “{name}” has a way to the network besides its Gateway
title.vmNet: The Gateway “{name}” changed its network traffic sharply
title.vmCpu: The machine “{name}” is using much more CPU than usual
title.vmMemory: The machine “{name}” is using much more memory than usual
why.vmScope: Its engine (QEMU) is no longer in the machine’s own group of limits: its CPU and memory limits no longer apply. Something on this computer moved it.
why.vmSandbox: Its engine runs without part of the sandbox that keeps the guest away from this computer: {missing}.
why.vmLeak: The Workstation of an anonymity group must reach the network only through its Gateway, but it has another way out: {paths}. Its traffic could reveal your real address.
why.vmNet: Its traffic or its number of connections jumped far above its own usual pattern.
why.vmCrash: It belongs to an anonymity group and stopped without being asked. {reason}
why.vmCrashLoop: Unexpected ends in the last {minutes} minutes: {n}. {reason}
why.vmCpu: It has used {avg} % of its processors for {minutes} minutes; it usually uses {base} %.
why.vmMemory: It uses {to} MB; it usually uses {base} MB.
path.network: its network setting isn’t the internal link
path.bridge: a bridge to a network card
trigger.vmUsage: Virtual machine using much more CPU or memory than usual
trigger.vmCrash: Virtual machine that crashes or keeps restarting
trigger.vmAnon: Anonymity group (Whonix): Gateway traffic that changes sharply, or a crash
trigger.vmAlways: Virtual machine that leaves its limits or loses its sandbox, or a Workstation with another way out
analysis.rule: Always shown: this alert needs no model.
settings.seesMachines: For virtual machines: their name, role and state, why they ended, and the CPU, memory and network counts of their engine. Never their screen, files or clipboard.
sandbox.unverified: proof that its engine is the machine’s own
block.endedBody: It is on your blocklist. Review the list in Settings → AI → Sentinela.
block.title: Blocklist
block.hint: These programs are ended whenever they start in your account, whether Sentinela is on or off. Add one from Monitor → Get Info → Investigate with Lumo; remove it to let it run again.
block.pkg: and every program of the package {pkg}
